sections.label: Who we are
sections.heading: Look for the system behind the symptom.
sections.body:
Fox Consulting Group is led by Justin Fuchs, who has spent nearly 20 years on the infrastructure side of marketing: strategy, analytics, platforms and the operating models that hold them together. Since 2016 the practice has delivered 30+ engagements for organizations including Aptiv, Altair, Corewell Health, Gordon Food Service and Allstate Identity Protection, and most clients have stayed five years or more.

Most recently, Justin built a hub-and-spoke analytics function across 13 business units at a public manufacturer, taking reporting from months to days. He’s as comfortable presenting a roadmap to a segment president as he is debugging the tag manager himself. You work with him directly, with a small bench of trusted specialists when the work calls for it.

servicePages.title: Digital Strategy Consulting
servicePages.heroSummary: Build a unified digital program that connects business priorities to channels, technology, measurement, and the work your team does every day.

problem.heading: Tactics move faster when the strategy underneath them is clear.
problem.body: Most teams do not need more ideas. They need a shared view of where digital marketing creates value, which opportunities deserve attention, and how people, process, and technology should work together. We turn that ambiguity into a practical operating roadmap.

capabilities.title: Channel planning
capabilities.body: Evaluate the channels that matter, clarify what each should accomplish, and build playbooks teams can actually use.

capabilities.title: Marketing technology strategy
capabilities.body: Assess the current stack and create a structured path for selecting, implementing, and governing the right tools.

capabilities.title: Leadership advisory

servicePages.title: Google Analytics 4 Consulting
servicePages.heroSummary: Turn GA4 from a source of uncertainty into a measurement system your team trusts, understands, and uses to make decisions.

problem.heading: A technically valid setup is not the same as useful analytics.
problem.body: GA4 often arrives with duplicated events, unclear conversions, broken governance, and reports no one confidently uses. We connect implementation decisions to the questions your organization actually needs analytics to answer.

capabilities.title: GA4 audits
capabilities.body: Review configuration, event design, conversions, data quality, governance, and reporting against your real measurement needs.

capabilities.title: Implementation planning
capabilities.body: Create an actionable measurement plan for GA4 and Google Tag Manager, including naming, ownership, and testing.

capabilities.title: Reporting systems
capabilities.body: Design focused reports and Looker Studio dashboards that make performance understandable to the people using them.

capabilities.title: Training and adoption
capabilities.body: Help marketers and leaders understand the platform, interpret data responsibly, and use it in recurring decisions.

approach.heading: Measure what matters, then make it usable.
approach.body: We begin with decisions and business questions—not a generic event checklist.

steps.title: Define
steps.body: Clarify the audiences, journeys, outcomes, and decisions the measurement system must support.

steps.title: Audit
steps.body: Inspect the current implementation and identify gaps, noise, risk, and unreliable reporting.

steps.title: Implement
steps.body: Configure, test, document, and govern a durable event and conversion framework.

steps.title: Operationalize
steps.body: Build reporting rhythms and train teams to turn analytics into action.

outcomes: A documented and governed measurement plan
Cleaner event and conversion data
Reports aligned to real stakeholder questions
Greater confidence and adoption across the marketing team

cta.heading: Make GA4 useful again.
cta.body: Whether you need an audit, a cleaner implementation, or help operationalizing analytics, we can clarify the next step.

servicePages.title: Privacy-Focused Marketing Analytics
servicePages.heroSummary: Build a useful marketing measurement program without treating privacy, consent, and data governance as afterthoughts.

problem.heading: Better privacy should lead to better measurement decisions.
problem.body: Regulation, browser changes, consent requirements, and sensitive customer data are reshaping analytics. We help teams determine what should be measured, what should not, and which platforms and governance practices fit their risk profile.

capabilities.title: Platform evaluation
capabilities.body: Compare Google Analytics, Piwik PRO, Matomo, and other approaches against privacy, security, reporting, and operational needs.

capabilities.title: Measurement governance
capabilities.body: Define standards for data collection, retention, access, documentation, and ongoing decision-making.

capabilities.title: Consent-aware implementation
capabilities.body: Align analytics architecture with consent requirements and the practical realities of your website and marketing stack.

capabilities.title: Privacy-first reporting
capabilities.body: Design reporting that remains useful even when individual-level tracking is limited or inappropriate.

approach.heading: Start with risk, value, and proportionality.
approach.body: There is no universal privacy stack. The right answer depends on your customers, markets, data sensitivity, and the decisions analytics must support.

steps.title: Frame
steps.body: Document business questions, regulatory context, data sensitivity, and organizational risk tolerance.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.body: Assess the current stack and compare viable platforms and implementation patterns.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: Create a measurement architecture and governance model that balances insight with restraint.

steps.title: Enable
steps.body: Support implementation, documentation, training, and ongoing stewardship.

outcomes: A defensible measurement strategy aligned to privacy requirements
Clear platform selection criteria
Documented ownership and data governance
Reporting that remains useful with less invasive tracking

cta.heading: Measure responsibly—and meaningfully.
cta.body: We can help you evaluate the tradeoffs and design a privacy-focused analytics program that fits your organization.

capabilities.title: Strategy review
capabilities.body: Bring a plan, roadmap, or recommendation and get direct, experienced feedback before you commit.

capabilities.title: Analytics troubleshooting
capabilities.body: Work through measurement questions, reporting gaps, platform choices, or implementation concerns.

capabilities.title: Technology decisions
capabilities.body: Clarify requirements, evaluation criteria, and tradeoffs before selecting or replacing marketing technology.

capabilities.title: Leadership coaching
capabilities.body: Use the session as a confidential thought partnership for organizational, team, or prioritization challenges.

approach.heading: Focused preparation. Candid advice. A usable next step.
approach.body: Each session is structured around one decision or challenge so the time produces a concrete outcome.

steps.title: Submit context
steps.body: Share the question, relevant background, and any materials that will make the conversation productive.

steps.title: Meet
steps.body: Use the session to examine assumptions, alternatives, risks, and practical next steps.

steps.title: Move
steps.body: Leave with a concise summary of recommendations and a clearer path forward.

outcomes: Independent perspective from a senior consultant
A clearer decision and immediate next step
No long-term engagement required
Advice grounded in your actual context

cta.heading: Bring the hard question.
cta.body: If a focused conversation would help you move forward, book an on-demand consulting session.

servicePages.title: Content Strategy Partnership for Developers
servicePages.heroSummary: Give website projects the strategic content leadership they need—without asking a development team to become a content agency.

problem.heading: Great builds still struggle when content strategy arrives too late.
problem.body: Development partners are often asked to solve messaging, information architecture, governance, and migration questions that sit outside their core role. Fox joins the project as a complementary content strategy partner, keeping the build focused and the client supported.

capabilities.title: Content discovery
capabilities.body: Clarify audiences, business objectives, stakeholder needs, and the role content must play in the new experience.

capabilities.title: Information architecture
capabilities.body: Shape navigation, page hierarchy, content models, and user pathways before templates harden.

capabilities.title: Page-level content strategy
capabilities.body: Define the purpose, priority, and content requirements for key page types and conversion journeys.

capabilities.title: Governance and migration
capabilities.body: Help clients decide what to keep, rewrite, retire, own, and maintain after launch.

approach.heading: A flexible partner inside your delivery model.
approach.body: We can work visibly alongside the client or quietly as an extension of your team, adapting to the project and relationship.

steps.title: Align
steps.body: Define roles, scope, decision rights, project milestones, and where content strategy adds the most value.

steps.title: Discover
steps.body: Lead stakeholder and audience work that gives design and development a stronger foundation.

steps.title: Structure
steps.body: Translate findings into architecture, content models, page requirements, and migration priorities.

steps.title: Support
steps.body: Stay engaged through design, build, content production, QA, and launch decisions.

outcomes: Clearer inputs for design and development
Fewer late-stage content surprises
Better alignment between templates and real content needs
A stronger client experience without expanding your core team

cta.heading: Add content strategy without adding overhead.
cta.body: Tell us how your team works and where content challenges tend to appear. We’ll shape a partnership around it.
